name: Chhattīsgarh
summary_text: Chhattisgarh mirrors Maharashtra's garba screening: in Bastar district, VHP and Bajrang Dal members objected to non-Hindu sponsors and participants at garba events, claiming damage to "cultural purity," and pressed religion-gated entry conditions — tilak applied to participants, Hanuman Chalisa recitation before start, and a Varaha-avatar poster circulated to organisers — with at least three garba nights called off and tickets cancelled after written objections; police received a memorandum and arranged venue security. It is the same outing mechanism as in Maharashtra, minus the Aadhaar document checks: a religion-screened gate at a public festival examines and outs gender-nonconforming visitors via actors who are not supposed to be involved. Unlike Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh has no constituted transgender welfare board (absent from the 12-state/UT list). Additionally, in November 2024 a transgender woman, Kajal (alias "Coca Cola"), was stabbed to death and dumped in an abandoned quarry in Baloda Bazar district in a Rs 12 lakh contract killing over rival claims to a community leadership seat ("guru gaddi") — a single incident with no sourced second instance, recorded for pattern awareness rather than as a decisive factor. Against the national 0.43, Chhattisgarh sits −0.06. The combination of festival-entrance screening (visitor-facing, seasonal, outing mechanism) and the absence of any state welfare apparatus distinguishes it from Maharashtra (0.38), which carries the same screening but at least has a board. Compared to Tripura (0.31), whose harm is state-police-driven border detention, Chhattisgarh's exposure is community-organiser-driven at private-adjacent festivals and the violence is a single unresolved incident. The gap to the national score is modest and confidence moderate.

sources.title: Garba nights in Bastar face objection, VHP, Bajrang Dal oppose non-Hindu sponsors & their participation | Raipur News - The Times of India
sources.claim_summary: Times of India, Raipur (23 Sep 2025): VHP and Bajrang Dal leaders in Bastar district objected to non-Hindu ("non-Sanatani") garba sponsors and participants as damaging "cultural purity", demanded tilak, Hanuman Chalisa recitation and a Varaha-avatar poster at venues, and warned of direct intervention; at least three garba nights were called off and tickets cancelled, a memorandum was filed with the administration, and police arranged venue deployment.

Times of India, Raipur (22 Nov 2024): transgender woman Kajal, alias "Coca Cola", was lured out, stabbed and dumped in an abandoned quarry at village Dhabadih (Baloda Bazar) in a Rs 12 lakh contract killing orchestrated by a rival, Tapasya, to block her ascent to the Jora Math community head seat ("guru gaddi"); five suspects were arrested and Rs 10.5 lakh seized.

sources.title: Constitution of Transgender Welfare Boards/Commissions
sources.claim_summary: Press Information Bureau reply in the Rajya Sabha (8 Dec 2021, Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar): 12 states/UTs have constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under section 10(1) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 - Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chandigarh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
